newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto family firm to build $2.45 bln road link.
newsitem.headline: Suharto family firm to build $2.45 bln road link.

text.p: A conglomerate controlled by one of Indonesian president Suharto's daughters will start building a 5.82 trillion rupiah ($2.45 billion) road-rail link in Jakarta in April, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.
The announcement is likely to end speculation on whether Jakarta, home to nearly 10 million people, would have a subway or elevated road-rail link to solve its chronic traffic problems.

Antara quoted Bambang Soeroso, chief executive officer of PT Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada, as saying on Sunday the multi-deck structure would consist of a 23.55 km (14.7 mile) toll road, a 21.25 km (13.2 mile) railway and a public road to link south Jakarta with downtown Kota in the north.
Officials for the firm or affiliated companies were not immediately available to provide further details.

PT Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada is controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana, 47, who is also involved in a long-running wrangle over Indonesia's Busang, one of the world's richest gold finds.
Rukmana also controls listed toll road operator PT Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada.

Soeroso said construction would start on April 21, the same day as a joint venture agreement between Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada and two state-owned companies, railway operator Perumka and toll road firm Jasa Marga was expected to be signed.
Antara said Perumka would use the railway track to link 22 stations to a light-rail commuter service while Jasa Marga would operate the toll road.
Newspapers reported in January that Transportation Minister Haryanto Dhanutirto had said only Perumka had the right to operate the light-rail commuter service.
Soeroso said 75 percent of the investment needed to construct the elevated transport corridor would come from loans, 40 percent of which would come from abroad.

He said a syndicate of 61 banks, including institutions from Hong Kong, Canada and Singapore as well as 51 domestic banks, would provide the loan. No further information was immediately available about the project's funding.
Soeroso said the flyover would start operation in 2001 and the toll road was expected to accommodate more than 100,000 vehicles a day.
